comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
So there are 2 issues here:

A) One is that you seem to have a corrupted segment file entry. The crc32 check failed for the entry in segment 1383 at offset 194962596.

This could be due to a hardware (usually RAM or storage medium) or kernel / filesystem error and is not related to borg.

**In case of a hw or fs issue, it is important to fix these first before trying to repair (as moving around a lot of data could cause more corruption).**

B) But, borg check has code to at least rescue the non-corrupt entries in a segment file, but that code is failing here:
```
  File "/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/borg/repository.py", line 1044, in check
    self.io.recover_segment(segment, filename)
  File "/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/borg/repository.py", line 1542, in recover_segment
    with mmap.mmap(src_fd.fileno(), 0, access=mmap.ACCESS_READ) as mm:
OSError: [Errno 19] No such device
```

Not sure what operation says "no such device" here, could be the `src_fd.fileno()` or the `mmap.mmap` or maybe the `__enter__` of that context manager opening.

But usually, that should work, so guess there is something malfunctioning below borg - maybe the mergerfs?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Usually `borg check --repair` can fix such issues (if it is just one or a few corrupted entries), but something in the stack **below borg** is malfunctioning here, maybe the fs or kernel.

The crc32 is computed and also checked by the repository code of borg, its main purpose is to detect corruption of the stored data / in the segment files used by borg.

Your repo URL does not look like borg is doing network stuff (no ssh:// repo), but you use some network fs and mergerfs. Thus, borg has nothing to do with the network transfer of the data and thus can't verify anything there.


Indirectly, if the repo resides on a network fs, the crc32 check will also detect corruption in the network fs part, so that might be what you are seeing here.

Maybe you could try a `borg check --repair --repository-only` of that repository using a simpler / more direct way. If invoked that way, it does not need the encryption key and could directly run on the server that has the repo storage.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Usually, if a borg create runs into a fatal error, it aborts the transaction. Next time borg is invoked, the incomplete transaction is rolled back to the last good state. But, as the docs point out, a disk full condition should be avoided by all means, because doing anything without any free disk space can be problematic.
